messages.subject: multiple composite variables
parts:
Hi,

It seems that as soon as I have more than one composite variable in my model, it becomes unidentified for reasons I can't pin point.

The very simplified version of my model is as follow:

#Saturated model
sat.mod = "
#Define the composite variables
#(plant1...6 refers to selected PCO axis [see main text for details])
#(pcnm1...45 refers to selected pcnm axes [see main text for details])

space <~ 1*pcnm3 + pcnm45 + pcnm1 + pcnm17 + pcnm2 + pcnm41 + pcnm9 + pcnm22 + pcnm6 + pcnm5
#plant.comp <~ 1*plant1 + plant2 + plant3 + plant4
herb.comp <~ 1*herb1 + herb2
#pred.comp <~ 1*pred1 + pred2 + pred3 + pred4 + pred5 + pred6

#Define regression paths
plant1 + plant2 + plant3 + plant4  ~ nitrogen + mowing  + space + herb.richness + herb.totab + herb.comp
"

sat.mod.fit  = sem(sat.mod,data=full.data,std.lv=T)

Warning message:
In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!
  lavaan NOTE: this may be a symptom that the model is not identified.


in theory, the sem function already fix the error variance for the composite variables to zero, so I do not understand what is wrong? Are there too many indicator variables per composite variables (my total number of observation is only 120)? Too many 0 in the co-variance matrix because each composite variable error variance is set to zero?

any tips or guidance would be greatly appreciated,
thanks!
Eric

parts:
On 01/21/2015 11:26 PM, harv...@hotmail.com wrote:
> Hi,
>
> It seems that as soon as I have more than one composite variable in my
> model, it becomes unidentified for reasons I can't pin point.

What about fixing the covariances between the composites to zero, eg. by
adding

space ~~ 0*herb.comp

If the (residual) variances are set to zero, there is no need for a
covariance term (which is added automatically).

Yves.
